pie: awis akwabʰyams ā wawakat: kard agʰnutai mai widanti manum akwams agantam.
english: The sheep said to the horses: "My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses."

pie: h₁ím kʷis ne wédʰeti dh₂pnóm-kʷe gʷm̥sḱéti. h₃rḗǵi h₂énti h₁ḗdti. wiHrṓs h₁ésmōd trésonti gʷénh₂es-kʷe HrudHénti. só múHs.
english: No one brings him, and he comes to the feast. He eats in front of the king. The heroes tremble before him, and the women cry aloud. He is the mouse.

pie: h₁ḗdti ne-kʷe wr̥ǵyéti. tód moy ne dayh₂wḗr. h₁yód wódr̥ píph₃ēti mért. dayh₂wḗr moy wódr̥ ne píph₃eti. tód péh₂wr̥.
english: It eats, and it does no work. It is not my brother-in-law. If it drinks water, it dies. My brother-in-law does not drink water. It is fire.

pie: kʷís dwóyh₁ lówksneh₂h₁ dyéwi dedórḱe? kʷís steh₂urṓy h₂roh₁dʰéyeti? kʷís dʰwóri h₂énti légʰeti h₁ésyo-kʷe gʷḗn h₁ím upér stéygʰeti? ph₃tós h₂nḗr.
english: Who sees two moons in the sky? Who talks to a stake? Who lies in front of the door, and his wife climbs over him? The drunk man.

pie: séne h₁eǵóh₂ deywós. gʷṓs moy toy dh₃dʰí. nu h₁íns sl̥h₂gʷdʰí. ḱwṓ moy deywós. h₁íns péh₂sti. só ne deywós. nu túH ne deywós. h₂epó gʷh₂dʰí.
english: Old man, I am a god. Give me your cattle! Then take them. My dog is a god. He guards them. He is not a god! Then you are not a god. Go away!

pie: pótey moy dayh₂wḗr wĺ̥kʷos. kʷíd léwbʰa tód bʰéh₂si? h₂ówins nos h₁ḗdti nékʷti-kʷe HréwdHti. ne HréwdHti gʷéHyeti. nu kʷíd gʰósteyes bʰugént?
english: Husband, my brother-in-law is a wolf. Why do you say that, beloved? He eats our sheep, and he cries aloud at night. He is not crying aloud; he is singing. Then why did the guests flee?

pie: kʷíd pótey dʰwórm̥ kapyési? pótni dʰéǵʰōm wértetor. dʰéǵʰōm ne wértetor. túH ph₃tós. nu kʷíd dwóyh₁ pótnih₂h₁ dedórḱh₂e? sméytes.
english: Husband, why are you clutching the door? The earth is turning, wife. The earth is not turning. You are drunk. Then why do I see two wives? The two of them are laughing.

pie: léymonm̥ dʰǵʰyés péh₃m̥. tósmi liméni dʰǵʰyés h₃méyǵʰom. nu wódr̥ swéh₂dt. ḱéywe túH ph₃tós.
english: Yesterday I drank a lake. Yesterday I was pissing in that lake. Then the water tasted good. You are drunk, dear friend.

pie: ǵr̥h₂n̥tés ǵn̥h₁yóh₂er. stéh₃mn̥ moy ne h₁ésti bʰéh₂mi-kʷe. gʰósteyes me ḱlush₁yónti litént-kʷe. ne kʷis me gʷr̥néHti. ǵérh₂onts pérdt.
english: I am born from an old man. I have no mouth, and I speak. The guests hear me and go away. No one praises me. The old man has farted.

pie: h₂wĺ̥pis spérm̥ h₁épt. spr̥sú h₂éǵt. h₂wĺ̥pey deywóns gʷr̥nHdʰí nu-kʷe me h₁ddʰí. h₂wĺ̥pis h₁íns gʷr̥néHt. spḗr h₁ésyeh₂s sth₃méns bʰéwgt. nu h₂wĺ̥pis mléwHt. h₁íns h₂ew ne gʷr̥néHoh₂.
english: The fox seized a sparrow. The sparrow said: "Fox, praise the gods, and then eat me!" The fox praised them. And the sparrow fled from her mouth. Then the fox said: "I will not praise them again."

pie: h₁súḱlewes toy h₁éḱwos HeHḱús. HeHḱús moy h₁éḱwos HeHḱús-kʷe h₁eǵóh₂. h₁éḱwos toy wĺ̥kʷōd dʰǵʰyés bʰéwgt túH-kʷe h₁ésmi h₁épi sísdes. ne bʰéwgm̥. wĺ̥kʷom ḱóymōd h₂epó wédʰom. sékʷeto te. sékʷeto-ge me.
english: Of-Good-Fame, your horse is swift. Swift is my horse, and swift am I. Yesterday your horse fled from the wolf, and you were sitting on it. I did not flee. I was leading the wolf away from the village. It was following you. It was following me indeed.

pie: wíHre gʷṓm h₂mélǵs? h₁súmenes h₁íh₂m̥ h₂mélǵm̥. nu kʷíd h₁ésyeh₂s h₁ówHdʰr̥ pléh₁dʰeti? nu kʷíd h₂mélǵm̥? káprom h₂mélǵs. gʰrémeti. ne gʰrémeti smḗyti.
english: Husband, did you milk the cow? I milked her, Kindly. Then why is her udder swelling? Then what did I milk? You milked the billy goat. He is angry. He is not angry; he is laughing.

pie: ǵérh₂ont moy wéwke. ḱósmi dinóy h₂wérseti? mógʰew h₂wérseti. kʷíh₁ wóydh₂e? wóydh₂e. pótnih₂ moy h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m h₂sowséyeti. h₁yód h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m h₂sowséyeti h₂wérst.
english: Elder, tell me: will it rain today? It will rain, boy. How do you know? I know. My wife is drying wool. When she dries wool, it rains.

pie: bʰṓr séneh₂s dʰwórm̥ nékʷti gʷémt. h₁íh₂ h₁ím ḱléwt. HréwdHt. pótey sth₂dʰí. gʷéru bʰére. dáyh₂weres gʷm̥té. bʰṓr h₂epó drémt. séneh₂ gʷḗn múHs-kʷe h₂én tḱitā́m.
english: A thief came by night to an old woman's door. She heard him. She cried aloud: "Husband, stand up!" "Bring the spear!" "Brothers-in-law, come!" The thief ran away. There lived the old woman and a mouse.

pie: gʰóstey h₁yós moysóns gʷr̥h₃ési. h₁yós-kʷe nos dʰrā́gʰm̥ píph₃esi. h₁yós nos str̥h₃méni légʰesi ḱludʰí nos. h₂én gʷh₂dʰí deywṓs toy h₁wésuh₂ h₂én dh₃ih₁ént.
english: Guest, you who devour the rams, and you who drink our dregs, you who lie on our bed, hear us! Go over there; may the gods give you good things over there.

pie: ǵérh₂onts pérkʷunom dh₂pnóy gʷr̥néHt. nu pérdt. h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs sméyn̥t. ǵérh₂onts sokʷéyet. mē sméyte. pérkʷunos gʰrémet. ḱléwt me. nu h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs pérkʷunom gʷr̥nHént.
english: At the sacrificial feast an elder was praising Perkʷunos. Then he farted loudly. The young men laughed. The elder said: "Do not laugh!" "Perkʷunos rumbled." "He heard me." Then the young men praised Perkʷunos.

pie: (h₁)éḱwōs ewewkʷ, "ḱludʰí, h₂ówi! ḱḗrd h₂gʰnutoy widntbʰós: dʰǵʰémō(n), pótis, h₂wlnéh₂m h₂ówyom kʷnewti sébʰoy gʷʰérmom wéstrom; h₂éwibʰoskʷe h₂wlh₂néh₂ né h₁esti."
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

pie: ph₂tḗr moy h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰént. ph₂tḗr moy dwóh₁ h₁ógʷʰih₁ ǵʰwḗrm̥-kʷe gʷʰént. ph₂tḗr moy ḱm̥tóm h₁ógʷʰins swóh₁ gʷrúh₁ gʷʰént. tód bʰebʰóydʰh₂e. méh₂tēr toy moy wéwket. muHsés dedwóye.
english: My father slew the serpent. My father slew two serpents and a wild beast. My father slew a hundred serpents with his spear. I trust that. Your mother told me: "He is afraid of a mouse."

pie: ǵénh₁tri moy h₂wl̥péys spélom wéwke. h₂wĺ̥pis ḱóymom nékʷti gʷémt. h₂ówis widét. nu kʷíd dʰéh₁t? h₁íh₂n̥s gʷr̥h₃ét. nu l̥gʰdʰí. h₂wl̥péys dedwóyh₂e. mē bʰéyh₂s. h₂wĺ̥pis medtéh₂.
english: Mother, tell me a story about the fox. The fox came to the village at night. She saw the sheep. What did she do then? She devoured them. Now lie down. I am afraid of the fox. Do not be afraid. The fox is full.

pie: h₂nŕ̥menes toy ḱléwos méǵh₂. HeHḱúm-ge múHsm̥ h₂Hséh₂h₁ ḱóm gʷʰéns. nu múHs légʰet túH-kʷe-ge tréms. h₂nŕ̥menes h₁ím gʷrúh₁ trís stunéds. wíHre toy ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom. bʰréh₂tēr toy swésōr-kʷe sméytes.
english: Man-Minded, great is your fame. You did slay the swift mouse beside the hearth. Then the mouse was lying down, and you indeed were trembling. Three times you struck it with the spear, Man-Minded. Hero, your fame is imperishable. Your brother and sister are laughing.

pie: h₂ówis, (H)yésmin h₂wlh₂néh₂ ne éh₁est, dedorḱe (h₁)éḱwons, tóm, wóǵʰom gʷérh₂um wéǵʰontm, tóm, bʰórom méǵoh₂m, tóm, dʰǵʰémonm h₂oHḱú bʰérontm.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: h₂wĺ̥pis wl̥kʷih₂éy wérh₁t. h₁yód gʷéHyesi h₂óweyes troméyonti. gʷh₂dʰí ḱóymoy-kʷe h₂énti gʷéHye. wl̥kʷíh₂s gʷéh₂t gʷéHyet-kʷe. poh₂iménes h₁íh₂m̥ ḱluwént dr̥mént-kʷe. h₂epó drémt. h₂wĺ̥pis moysóm h₂én h₁épt. nu h₂wĺ̥pis h₂éǵt. wĺ̥kʷih₂ h₂ew gʷéHye. moysós swéh₂dt.
english: The fox said to the she-wolf: "When you sing, the sheep tremble." "Go and sing by the village!" The she-wolf went and sang. The shepherds heard her and ran. She ran away. On the other side, the fox seized a ram. Then the fox said: "She-wolf, sing again!" "The ram was tasty."

pie: bʰṓr h₁ésyeh₂s bʰebʰóyh₂e h₁ésyeh₂s pótis h₁ésyeh₂s bʰebʰóyh₂e. h₁yód múHsm̥ widḗtes HréwdHti kʷékʷlom-kʷe h₁épi stéygʰeti. kʷís séh₂? séh₂ pótnih₂.
english: The thief fears her; her husband fears her. When she sees a mouse, she cries aloud and climbs onto the cart. Who is she? She is the wife.

pie: kʷís wíHre dh₂pnóm h₂éḱh₃t? ḱéywa múHs tód h₂éḱh₃t. múHs méǵh₂ dh₂pnóm gʷr̥h₃ét? nu bʰindtó. bʰindtó-ge. nu str̥h₃méni ḱéyor. túH só múHs.
english: Husband, who ate up the feast? A mouse ate it up, dear. A mouse devoured a great feast? Then it burst! It did burst. Now it is lying on the bed. You are that mouse!

pie: ph₃tós h₂nḗr lówksneh₂m liméni widét. lówksneh₂ léymonm̥ séngʷt h₂éǵt. léymonm̥ péh₃oh₂ lówksneh₂m-kʷe spéroh₂. nókʷtm̥ pér píph₃et. h₂wést lówksneh₂-kʷe néḱt. ḱóymom gʷéh₂t wéwket-kʷe. pótni lówksneh₂m péh₃m̥. nu h₁eǵóh₂ medtós.
english: A drunk man saw the moon in the lake. "The moon has sunk into the lake!" he said. "I will drink the lake and free the moon." He drank through the night. It grew light, and the moon vanished. He went home and said: "Wife, I drank the moon." "Now I am full."

pie: bʰréh₂ter pṓlHom dʰǵʰyés tl̥nā́m. h₁éḱwom tl̥nā́m. dwóh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁ kʷékʷlom-kʷe tl̥nā́m. dʰéǵʰōm tl̥nā́m. nu kúdʰe sth₂éh₁yes? bʰréh₂ter toy kólsoy h₁épi sth₂éh₁yom. ne widés?
english: Brother, yesterday I lifted a foal. I lifted a horse. I lifted two horses and a wagon. I lifted the earth. Then where were you standing? I was standing on your neck, brother. Did you not notice?

pie: múHses bʰréh₂teres HrudHtóm. sénos nos gʰóstis ḱóymom gʷémt. dh₂pnóm h₂éḱh₃t h₂éHsh₂m̥-kʷe léyǵʰt. nu-kʷe kʷid n̥sméy ne h₁ésti. kénkomes h₂éǵrom bʰéwgomes.
english: Mice, brothers, cry aloud! The old guest has come to our home. He ate up the feast and licked the hearth. And now there is nothing for us. We are hungry; let us flee to the field!

pie: súHnew h₂wést. sth₂dʰí. ph₂ter memónh₂e. kʷíd memónth₂e? kʷís h₂éǵrom h₂érh₃yēti? túH h₁ím h₂érh₃yēsi. nu h₂ew légʰoh₂.
english: It has dawned, son. Get up! Father, I am thinking. What are you thinking? Who will plough the field? You will plough it! Then I will lie down again.
